work.text: One of his many works from his series of Nocturnes, it is the last of the London Nocturnes and is now widely acknowledged to be the high point of Whistler's middle period.

moment.text: I have seen, and heard, much of Cockney impudence before now; but never expected to hear a coxcomb ask two hundred guineas for flinging a pot of paint in the public's face.
moment.lead: John Ruskin, reviewing the Grosvenor Gallery exhibition in Fors Clavigera, July 1877:

moment.text: He looked at The Falling Rocket, and was blind to the beauty and to the mastery of the painter.

moment.text: Nonetheless, the jury reached a verdict in favor of Whistler, but a farthing—the smallest unit of currency—was awarded in nominal damages, and the court costs were split.

matters.text: No! Do you know I fear it would be as hopeless as for the musician to pour his notes into the ear of a deaf man.

matters.text: The cost of the case, together with huge debts from building his residence ("The White House" in Tite Street, Chelsea, designed with E. W. Godwin, 1877–8), bankrupted him by May 1879, resulting in an auction of his work, collections, and house.
